study.title: Clinical practice patterns and unmet needs in the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in sleep medicine: A pan-European survey performed in the European sleep apnoea database network

cover.headline: Weight-loss drugs are arriving in sleep clinics, but **no one agrees on how to use them**.

slides.title: GLP-1 drugs reduce weight and sleep apnoea severity, but real-world clinical practice remains undefined.
slides.body:
Tirzepatide and similar medications recently gained regulatory approval for obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity. Sleep medicine is starting to integrate these drugs into treatment, but there are no agreed protocols.

The European Sleep Apnoea Database network surveyed 24 centres across 14 countries to map current practice patterns, diagnostic timing, and how clinicians manage airway pressure therapy when patients lose weight on these medications.

slides.title: Forty-two percent of centres allow sleep physicians to prescribe GLP-1 drugs directly within the clinic.
slides.body:
Most clinicians still recommend diagnostic sleep studies in both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients recently started on GLP-1 therapy—92% and 81%, respectively. Sixty-one percent of centres consider weight loss above 10% a meaningful threshold for reassessing sleep apnoea.

Despite expecting reductions in apnoea severity, only 14% of centres proactively re-titrate or withdraw positive airway pressure therapy. Monitoring focuses on weight trajectory, symptoms, and telemonitoring data, but structured interdisciplinary pathways are largely absent.

caveats: This survey captured practice patterns at one point in time, not whether any approach works better.
Industry funding supported part of this work, which is worth noting when interpreting the findings.

caption: GLP-1 receptor agonists are moving into European sleep medicine, but practice varies wildly across centres. The ESADA network surveyed 24 sleep centres in 14 countries. Indications were consistent—moderate-to-severe obesity with metabolic comorbidities—but follow-up strategies and airway pressure management diverged sharply. Most centres lack structured interdisciplinary pathways despite the complexity of managing both weight-loss therapy and sleep apnoea treatment. Published in Pulmonology, based on responses from clinicians at European sleep centres. This is a snapshot of practice, not a test of outcomes. Full study: doi.org/10.1080/25310429.2026.2722795 — Does your clinic use GLP-1s?
